test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On 10 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Some colleagues at a workplace are really __hard nuts to crack.__

options.text: An inflexible person who is hard to convince
Someone showing extra concern over little things
An easy-goer who can be easily convinced

solution:
The correct answer is ** An inflexible person who is hard to convince.****​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom is **An inflexible person who is hard to convince.**
 
• **Hard nut to crake **means **anything or someone that is challenging to deal with.**
 
• Thus the correct answer is An inflexible person who is hard to convince.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Related to hard nut to crake but words- **without a hitch, take a crack at, tough nut, slipping through the cracks.**
 
• Examples -*** I've been dating Jenny for over a year, and I still think she's a hard nut to crack!***
 
 
• ***​This problem is getting me down. It's a hard nut to crack.***
